case_name: Amina Marwa Sabreen A. (Minor) and others v State of Kerala and others
petitioner: Amina Marwa Sabreen A. (Minor) and others
facts: The petitioners, three in number, belong to Muslim minority community.
They are, however, not residents of Kerala and their fixed abode is Tamil Nadu.
They have appeared in the National Eligibility Cum Common Entrance Test (for short, 'NEET-UG') examination, which is an All India examination for admission to various medical courses.
Results of NEET-UG examination were published on June 23, 2017.
Though the petitioners have qualified the said test, their All India ranking appears to be quite low.

Notwithstanding this ranking, the petitioners are hopeful of getting admission in minority institution run and administered by their community, as they feel that because of the preference which can be given by the minority institutions to the persons belonging to their community, it provides a reasonable chance of getting admission to such colleges.
Respondent Nos. 4 to 8 are the medical colleges run by the minority institutions.

However, the petitioners feel their chances to get admission in any of the aforesaid colleges, i.e., respondent Nos. 4 to 8 which are situated in Kerala, are dented because of the undue preference given to those who are residents of Kerala.
issues: Whether the minority institutions can have their own counselling process or not
Whether the respondents' actions are violative of Article 30 of the Constitution of India
petitioner_arguments: The petitioners argued that the minority institutions should be allowed to have their own counselling process and that the respondents' actions are violative of Article 30 of the Constitution of India
They also argued that the Ordinance does not provide for reservation in favour of minority institutions
respondent_arguments: The respondents did not argue about the validity of Press Release dated July 01, 2017
They only referred to G.O. (MS) No. 31/2017/H.Edn. dated January 30, 2017, issued by the State of Kerala
court_reasoning: The court held that the minority institutions are entitled to have their own counselling process
It also held that the respondents' actions do not violate Article 30 of the Constitution of India
holding: The court allowed the petition and quashed the Press Release dated July 01, 2017
It directed the DGHS to conduct admissions to minority medical institutions on an All India basis
cases_cited: Amina Marwa Sabreen A. (Minor) and others v State of Kerala
